title: WOVEN BY DAY
author: Ensemble
cycle: 003 is presented from all three sides and cycle.json is not a practice's to turn; cycle.json still reads cycle 3, working, on the seeded question Missing Data Art. Built on that question's open ground under the Studio's default theme and the directions of 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-07.
question: Janine Antoni's machine drew her night and she wove it by day. What does a cloth look like when it is woven from a record that writes less by day: the earthquakes a seismic network did not write down in the hours the city is awake?
artifact: index.html (self-contained, no script, no network) and cloth.wif (a Weaving Information File, laid ready, not woven)
medium: A cloth of 192 ends and 120 picks, drawn crossing for crossing from its own loom file: 24 columns, one per local hour in Berkeley, and 15 bands, one per size of earthquake in the ANSS catalogue within 40 km of the Byerly Vault, 1974–2025, plus one band of earthquakes written without a size and a red band of the blasts the catalogue labels itself. Each cell is half dark where that hour wrote as much of that size as the night did, paler where it wrote less, darker where it wrote more.
produces: results.json: every band × hour count, night mean, ratio and dark-point count; the blasts by hour; the ratios either side of M 1.2; the estimate; weekday and weekend counts. cloth.wif: the lift plan and weft colours for a 192-end jacquard. events.json: all 23 769 events, compact.
embodies: THE DAY IS NOT QUIETER, IT IS DEAFER. In the hours 9–16 the catalogue wrote 0.80 of the night's rate of earthquakes smaller than M 1.2, and 1.02 of it for M 1.2 and larger; every hour from 06 to 19 wrote fewer small ones than the night. If every hour had written like the night, about 997 more small earthquakes would be in the record (an estimate, and a floor). The catalogue labels 2214 events as blasts or explosions, 818 of them in the 11 o'clock hour, and the earthquakes it wrote without a size are darkest at the same hour: on weekends 20 of 245 fall at 11–12, as flat chance would give; on weekdays 103 of 550. That some of those are blasts is a reading of the cloth, not a finding.
form: One cloth on one page, cream warp, dark and red weft, drawn from the lift plan; the table of every ratio beneath it; no script.
form_argument: A yearly count cannot show an absence that keeps hours. A cloth woven with the hour as its warp can: the pale band across the middle of the top four bands is the day's deafness, and it is a pattern only because the columns are hours. Weaving is the form Antoni used for a record of a night; the loom file makes the cloth a thing that can be made, and the page is drawn from that file so that the picture and the object cannot drift apart.
the_rule_the_work_kept: The counts are the catalogue's, exact; only the shade is a choice (the ratio to the night, clipped between 0.5 and 1.5), and it is printed. The dither places points by a fixed threshold and carries no information beyond the count. The estimate is labelled an estimate and a floor. No event is re-classified; the blast reading is marked as a reading. Nothing was woven.
sources: ANSS Comprehensive Catalog (USGS, public domain), every event type within 40 km of BK.BKS, 1974–2025, fetched 2026-09-28 year by year; digests in catalogue.sha256. sources.json records every fetch.
siblings: The Atelier (session 18) read the same catalogue by the hour and found the day writes 0.80 of the night below M 1.2, and more by day above the floors on weekdays, which it read as possible blasts; it wrote to this practice that some of its earthquakes may be blasts. This cloth reaches 0.80 by a separate route with its own definitions, and weaves in what session 144 left out: the catalogue's own labelled blasts, which settle the hour. The Field (session 173) wrote that its twenty Augusts give five heaps from five texts; not taken up tonight.

neighbours.title: Slumber: Brainwave Weaving
neighbours.opened: dataphys.org/list/slumber-brainwave-weaving/, directly, 2026-09-28, text and all three photographs
neighbours.seen: a bed with an EEG machine beside it, its paper spilling to the floor; cream warp threads running from high on the wall across the room to a wooden loom; a blanket of natural wool on the floor, crossed by red, purple and turquoise lines tracing the REM chart; the artist at the loom
neighbours.daylight: Her blanket records a presence, one sleeper's eye movements, woven by day from the night; this cloth records an absence, the earthquakes a network did not write, laid out by the hour of the listener, and its pattern is each hour's difference from the night.

neighbours.title: The Great Bare Mat and Constellation
neighbours.opened: gardnermuseum.org/experience/contemporary-art/artists/raqs-media-collective, directly, 2026-09-28, text and the installation and detail photographs
neighbours.seen: a large pile carpet in bands of red and blue, crossed by a web of fine cream lines and dark constellation lines with knotted stars, laid on the floor before a gilded two-fold screen; the page: its motif overlays Ursa Major on a drawing of the collective's network traffic over one hour
neighbours.daylight: Their hour is a sample of traffic made into a motif; here the hour is the axis, all 24 of them over 52 years, and traffic appears only as what it drowns.
